Title: IOTC purse seine data workshop
Executing agencies / staff:
IOTC Data Coordinator 
IOTC Fishery Officer 
IOTC National Profession Officer 
EU, Kenya,  Mozambique, Seychelles, Mauritius and Tanzania
Description of activities: The IOTC purse seine data reporting workshop, held in Seychelles in March 2026, brought together 18 participants from six CPCs to strengthen reporting on purse seine fisheries, including mandatory statistical datasets, drifting floating object (DFOB) data, and Regional Observer Scheme (ROS) reporting. The workshop improved participants' understanding of IOTC reporting requirements, facilitated the exchange of national experiences and challenges, and identified key data gaps and priorities for consideration by the WPDCS and WPEB.
Summary: The workshop brought together 18 participants from six CPCs to strengthen the reporting of purse seine fisheries data. It covered mandatory statistical reporting forms, including catches, discards, species interactions, size data and drifting floating objects (DFOBs), as well as ROS reporting requirements and tools. Discussions also addressed national data reporting workflows, persistent data gaps and opportunities to improve data quality and reporting.

Title: Data support mission in Comoros
Executing agencies / staff: IOTC Data Coordinator; IOTC National Professional Officer
Description of activities:
The mission was organised by the IOTC Secretariat as part of ongoing capacity development activities, through which Comoros was identified as one of the CPCs with limited data processing capabilities.
The objectives of the mission were to:
 (1) assess the data processing systems of Comoros, including the data collection, storage, and processing mechanisms in use, 
(2) follow up on the systems implemented under the World Bank project that concluded in 2021,
 (3) identify the most appropriate approaches to improve the existing systems, and
 (4) review the data available to assess whether Comoros could be considered as a case-study for the activity focusing on coastal fishery data processing planned under the EU-funded project EC1350.
Summary: The mission assessed fisheries data collection, storage and processing systems in Comoros, including follow-up on systems developed under the World Bank project completed in 2021. It also identified opportunities to strengthen data management and evaluated the potential for Comoros to serve as a case study for coastal fisheries data processing under the EU-funded project EC1350.

Title: Data support mission in Comoros
Executing agencies / staff: IOTC Fisheries officer (data); IOTC National Profession Officer
Description of activities:
During the WPDCS21, Tanzania requested the Secretariat assistance to review the ongoing work on the data management and further training to related to the challenges faced in data reporting. The main objectives of the mission in Tanzania were to: 
 - review the proposed methodology for the historical catch reconstruction of artisanal fisheries; 
 - assess the progress made in implementing harmonised fisheries data management processes among the different entities; and 
 - provide feedback on the latest submission, with a focus on industrial fisheries data reporting requirements.
Summary: The mission identified several priority actions to strengthen fisheries data management, including the reporting requirements of the main datasets and ROS. Refinement of the catch reconstruction presentation for WPDCS22, and the Secretariat is available for any assistance.

Title: Data support mission in Tanzania
Executing agencies / staff: IOTC Fisheries officer (data);  IOTC National Profession Officer
Summary: The mission provided technical support and hands-on training to Kenya Fisheries Service officers on IOTC data reporting requirements and tools, including e-MARIS and the Regional Observer Scheme (ROS). Discussions reviewed existing fisheries datasets, progress in developing a harmonised national fisheries data management system, and opportunities to strengthen data collection, historical catch estimates and reporting through continued capacity building and collaboration with national stakeholders.

Title: ROS longline data reporting worshop
Executing agencies / staff:
IOTC Fishery Officer 
EU, Indonesia, Maldives, China, Taiwan,China, Malaysia, South Africa and Tanzania
Description of activities: The ROS longline data reporting workshop was held from 26th-29th May 2026 in Johannesburg, South Africa counting with 12 participants from 8 CPCs and invited experts.
Summary: The workshop brought together 12 participants from eight CPCs to strengthen ROS data reporting for longline fisheries. It reviewed reporting requirements, available tools and historical data gaps, with particular emphasis on improving data quality and reconstructing historical submissions using standardised IOTC forms. Discussions also covered national observer programmes, electronic monitoring systems, the e-MARIS platform and the development of data validation tools, with CPCs providing feedback on priorities for further improvements.

Title: Annual meeting of the EU RCG on Large Pelagics
Description of activities: Presentation of a summary on data needs and gaps regarding large pelagic data in the IOTC, with a summary of EU data reporting status.
Summary: The IOTC Secretariat participated in the annual meeting of the EU Regional Coordination Group for Large Pelagics (RCG-LP), presenting IOTC data reporting requirements and an assessment of EU Member States' data submissions, highlighting outstanding data gaps and inconsistencies. The presentation also covered ongoing improvements to data validation procedures, drifting fish aggregating device (DFAD) reporting and Regional Observer Scheme (ROS) data management, emphasising opportunities for collaboration with EU scientific institutes to improve data quality and reporting.

Title: ISSF technical data workshop
Description of activities: ISSF Workshop on the Importance of Tropical Tuna Fisheries of Large  and Small Scales
Summary: The workshop brought together experts from tuna RFMOs, FAO, scientists, and stakeholders to examine the role and impacts of small-scale (SSF), intermediate-scale, and large-scale fisheries targeting tropical tunas. Participants sought to improve the consistency of definitions, strengthen fisheries data, evaluate fishery impacts, and identify governance improvements that support science-based management.

Title: Indian Ocean shark research plan workshop
Description of activities: Preparing and presenting the dataset at Shark research plan workshop
Summary: The workshop reviewed available shark data and identified major gaps in fisheries statistics, particularly for coastal and gillnet fisheries. Recommendations focused on strengthening species-level reporting, improving national data collection systems through targeted capacity building, recovering unpublished datasets and biological samples, and investigating discrepancies between reported catches and trade statistics. These priorities contributed to the development of a research roadmap to improve shark data availability and support stock assessments and management within the IOTC.

Title: Data support mission in Madagascar
Executing agencies / staff: IOTC Fisheries officer; IOTC National Professional Officer
Description of activities:
The visit was principally to follow-up on last year mission, development so far, and to evaluate the sampling data collection systems with the posilibity of Madagascar participating in the data biological sampling project. The objectives of the mission were to: 
 - Evaluating the sampling system ability to participate in IOTC biological system program 
 - Assessing Madagascar’s data collection, recording, and processing systems, including the use of electronic tools 
- Identifying data gaps and understanding the factors contributing to inconsistencies in reported data 
- Evaluating the most effective approaches for processing and reporting fisheries data 
- Assessing third party contributions to the national data collection effort.
Summary: The mission reviewed Madagascar’s fisheries data collection and management systems through discussions with national authorities, fisheries officers and other stakeholders, complemented by visits to landing sites. It identified opportunities to strengthen national sampling strategies, harmonise data collection procedures and develop integrated electronic data management systems, with continued technical support and capacity-building activities planned in collaboration with the IOTC Secretariat.

Title: EU fisheries data collection  liaison meeting
Description of activities: European Commission Fisheries Data Collection  Liaison Meeting Enduser
Summary: The IOTC Secretariat participated in the EU Regional Coordination Group liaison meeting as an end-user of fisheries data, presenting IOTC reporting requirements, the status of EU fleet data submissions and remaining data gaps, particularly for bycatch and discards. Discussions also covered ongoing improvements to data validation, reporting forms and information systems, as well as opportunities to strengthen collaboration with EU data collectors and scientific institutes to improve data quality, consistency and accessibility.

Title: Data support mission in Oman
Executing agencies / staff: IOTC Data Coordinator; IOTC Fisheries officer
Summary: The mission reviewed Oman’s fisheries data collection, processing and reporting systems through technical discussions with the Ministry of Agriculture, Fisheries and Water Resources and visits to landing sites and the Central Fish Market. Practical training was provided on IOTC reporting requirements, while discussions focused on improving sampling and catch estimation methods, strengthening species identification and supporting the development of integrated fisheries data management systems, with further technical assistance and capacity-building activities planned.

Title: ICCAT technical workshop on bycatch data
Description of activities: Revision of the Sub-committee's Data Collection and Research Program (PIRDCaF) - Joint RFMo group : Fisheries Bycatch : Shared Priorities and Global Action Projects
Summary: The IOTC Secretariat participated in technical discussions organised by ICCAT on bycatch data collection and reporting, including the availability and quality of observer data, species identification and reporting standards. The exchanges provided an opportunity to share information on common data challenges and approaches to improving bycatch statistics across tuna RFMOs.

Title: Regional and national ALDFG reporting frameworks
Summary: The IOTC Secretariat participated in technical webinars organised by FAO and SEAFDEC in preparation for a regional workshop on reporting abandoned, lost or otherwise discarded fishing gear (ALDFG) in Southeast and South Asia. The webinars reviewed international, regional and national reporting frameworks, including requirements under tuna RFMOs, and explored opportunities to harmonise data collection and reporting procedures to support the development of regional guidelines and reporting templates.

Title: ROS gillnet data workshop
Description of activities: Review of alternative data collection methods for gillnet fisheries under the IOTC Regional Observer Scheme (ROS)
Summary: The IOTC Secretariat organised an online workshop on alternative data collection methods for gillnet fisheries under the Regional Observer Scheme (ROS). The workshop reviewed existing reporting requirements and national data collection programmes, including crew-based observer initiatives, and provided an opportunity to discuss challenges and potential approaches to harmonising data collection and reporting practices across CPCs.
